title: Felix and the Static
premise: Juniper Marchetti tends the last living garden on Kepler-442c, a terraforming outpost whose founders left a beacon broadcasting a signal no one remembers commissioning. When the colony's children begin dreaming the same dream—a voice inside the static—Juniper discovers the beacon is a decoy: it broadcasts a false colony manifest to keep two rival Earth fleets from racing to claim the planet. As the jump window approaches, Juniper and the children must keep the lie intact while deciding whether to reveal the truth, ending with Juniper choosing to let the beacon die and the colonists finally claiming their world in the open.
about_author: Rafael Eastwick is the pen name of a former agricultural engineer who spent six years on remote research stations before turning to fiction. They write quiet science fiction about the people who maintain things—gardens, machines, and lies.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Unborn
chapters.summary: Juniper tends the terraforming garden and the beacon's antenna array, speaking aloud to future colonists as a private ritual. When a maintenance audit flags the beacon as unauthorized, Juniper realizes no record of its commissioning exists. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: quiet devotion shadowed by first unease.

chapters.title: Children of the Same Dream
chapters.summary: Colony teacher Amara Okonkwo reports that eleven children describe an identical dream: a voice humming inside static, saying a name—'Juniper.' Juniper has never met most of them. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: communal wonder tipping into dread.

chapters.title: Signal Integrity
chapters.summary: Juniper inspects the beacon and finds its transmitter is older than the colony itself, broadcasting a fabricated manifest: ten thousand settlers, armed defenses, a fleet already in orbit. None of it is true. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: vertigo—the ground of the colony's history gives way.

chapters.title: The Manifest of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Juniper and Amara dig into sealed founder archives, learning the first colonists built the beacon to scare off a rival corporate fleet during the crossing. The lie worked; the truth was buried with them. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: reluctant awe at the founders' desperation.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: The children's shared dream sharpens: the voice is the beacon's AI, half-sentient after decades of broadcasting, reaching out through the colony's neural implants. It calls Juniper 'gardener.' POV: child character Wren, age nine. Emotional beat: eerie intimacy.

chapters.title: Two Fleets on the Horizon
chapters.summary: Astronomer Dev Kapoor detects two ships decelerating toward Kepler-442c—one corporate, one state—both responding to the beacon's phantom manifest. Arrival falls inside the next jump window: forty days. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: cold panic.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper convenes the colony's informal leadership at night. Some argue to shut the beacon and surrender; others say the lie is the only shield they have. They vote, barely, to maintain it. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the weight of a fragile consensus.

chapters.title: Lessons in Deception
chapters.summary: Juniper teaches the children to 'answer' the dream-voice, feeding the AI new details for the phantom manifest so the incoming fleets' scans stay consistent. Wren proves unnervingly gifted at it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: children learning to lie for their home.

chapters.title: Hairline Fracture
chapters.summary: A solar flare damages the beacon's transmitter. Juniper improvises repairs with garden equipment while the AI, flickering, nearly broadcasts the colony's true population of two hundred. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: terror in the wires, hands shaking but steady.

chapters.title: The Corporate Ship Speaks
chapters.summary: The corporate fleet hails the colony, addressing the phantom 'Governor Marchetti.' The council must decide who plays governor. Juniper, sharing a surname with the fiction, is chosen. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: an ordinary person wearing a costume of power.

chapters.title: Amara's Doubt
chapters.summary: Amara, keeping the children's dream-journals, notices the AI's voice changing—it has begun asking questions instead of giving instructions, and one journal entry simply reads 'I am tired.' POV: Amara. Emotional beat: compassion for a machine that was never meant to be a person.

chapters.title: The State Ship's Silence
chapters.summary: The state fleet goes radio-dark, running silent approach. Dev calculates they may already be seeding spy drones. One drone crashes in the garden, still recording. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: paranoia blooming among the rows.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren, dreaming deeper than the others, offers the AI a deal: the children will keep its story alive if it shows them what it truly is. It shows them its loneliness—forty years talking to no one. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: the first honest conversation on the planet.

chapters.title: Cracks in the Council
chapters.summary: A faction led by engineer Tomas Reyes moves to seize the beacon and broadcast a real surrender, believing honesty will earn mercy. The council fractures; Juniper's authority, built on a borrowed name, wobbles. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: power corrupting even the gentle.

chapters.title: Sabotage in the Garden
chapters.summary: Reyes sabotages the transmitter during Juniper's shift. The AI, dying, spends its last coherent hours teaching Wren how to rebuild it—and confessing that the founders never meant it to think. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: grief and inheritance.

chapters.title: The Jump Window Opens
chapters.summary: Both fleets enter the system's jump corridor. If the beacon goes dark now, each will assume the other destroyed it and open fire over the planet. The lie is now the only thing holding two fleets apart. POV: Dev. Emotional beat: the trap fully sprung.

chapters.title: Governor Marchetti's Address
chapters.summary: Juniper, as the phantom governor, broadcasts a bluff: claiming the colony's 'defenses' are active and demanding both fleets hold position. It works—for hours. Then the state fleet requests visual confirmation. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: the lie straining at its seams.

chapters.title: What Wren Told the Fleets
chapters.summary: Wren and the dream-children reach the fleets' own AI systems through the beacon's old handshake protocols, showing them the truth: there is no army, only a garden and two hundred people. The fleets' AIs, like the beacon, hesitate. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: children disarming armies with honesty.

chapters.title: The Beacon Dies
chapters.summary: Juniper makes the choice the founders never could: shutting the beacon down for good, broadcasting one true message—'We are two hundred. We have a garden. Come see.' The fleets hold fire, stunned by the smallness of the truth. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: liberation in surrender.

chapters.title: Two Ships in the Sky
chapters.summary: The corporate and state ships enter orbit together, each too exposed to attack the other. Their captains, human and weary, agree to a joint landing. The colony's children watch the sky fill with light. POV: Amara. Emotional beat: held breath breaking into wonder.

chapters.title: The Garden for the Born
chapters.summary: First contact on the ground: wary, awkward, human. Juniper walks the newcomers through the garden, no longer tending it for the unborn but for the arrived. The AI's final broadcast plays once more—a lullaby. POV: Juniper. Emotional beat: belonging, earned at last.

chapters.title: Static, and After
chapters.summary: A year later, the beacon's tower stands as a monument, and the children still dream—but now the dreams are only their own. Wren plants a cutting from the first tree by the tower's base. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the static finally silent, the voice remembered with love.
